slides.title: MuVAP: Multimodal Multiparty Voice Activity Projection for Turn-taking Prediction in the Wild
slides.highlight: MuVAP uses a causal multimodal framework to enable speaker-aware turn-taking predictions from a single camera and monaural audio, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: MuVAP predicts multiparty turn-taking using a single camera and monaural audio via role-relative projections.
card.key_idea: Grounds acoustic voice activity projections in face tracks using Role-Relative Projection, mapping N-speaker dynamics onto a fixed 'current vs. next' floor-holder state for social scalability.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the new 31-hour AVCC dataset using Shift-Hold (Macro-F1) and Next Speaker Prediction (Accuracy) tasks; outperformed MLP and unimodal baselines.
card.limitation: Performance is lower in 'active' prediction tasks compared to 'silent' ones and decreases as speaker count increases.

slides.title: WaveSync: Constrained Wavefront Optimization for Synchronized Co-Speech Gestures in Humanoid Robots
slides.tldr: SYNCHRONIZED CO-SPEECH GESTURES FOR HUMANOID ROBOTS
slides.highlight: WaveSync uses a hybrid framework and LLMs to align expressive gestures with speech while ensuring kinematic feasibility. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: WaveSync synchronizes humanoid robot gestures with speech emphasis while respecting strict physical kinematic constraints.
card.key_idea: An LLM generates a Semantic Importance Wave; DMPs shape trajectories, and a wavefront optimizer aligns gesture peaks to speech peaks using duration compression and forward propagation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via PyBullet simulations across five scenarios using objective metrics (HbS, PAM, Jerk) and subjective Likert ratings from 20 participants; outperformed three ablated baselines.
card.limitation: Relies on a fixed action library, limiting its ability to handle unconstrained dialogue; not yet tested on physical hardware.

slides.title: Beyond Usability: A UX Case Study on Using "Withdrawal Design" to Challenge Engagement Metrics in Social Robotics
slides.tldr: CHALLENGING ENGAGEMENT METRICS IN SOCIAL ROBOTICS
slides.highlight: This study examines how the removal of a social robot can prompt children with autism to seek human interaction, suggesting that high engagement may sometimes silo social behavior. It is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: Withdrawal of social robots may better promote human social motivation than continued robot engagement.
card.key_idea: A mixed-methods "withdrawal design" comparing children who kept a social robot versus those who had it removed to assess long-term human-centric social gains.
card.evaluation: 8-week home RCT (N=40) using SCARED, RCADS, SMS, RMET, and SUS metrics; results show a trade-off between anxiety reduction and social motivation.

slides.title: UBTECH launches UWORLD U1 humanoid robot companions
slides.highlight: The launch of UWORLD U1 humanoid robot companions is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Tuning Agent-Based Predator-Prey Models Toward Lotka-Volterra Dynamics
slides.tldr: TUNING AGENT-BASED MODELS FOR STABLE POPULATION DYNAMICS
slides.highlight: This research explores tuning parameters in agent-based models with neural network controllers to achieve stable population oscillations, supporting MIMIC's focus on meso- and societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: Tuning agent-based predator-prey parameters using a macroscopic loss to achieve Lotka-Volterra-like population oscillations.
card.key_idea: A JAX-based ABM with CTRNN controllers is optimized via CMA-ES using a feature-based loss rewarding lagged correlations, bounded populations, and sustained oscillations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using random and evolved controllers; results show successful emergence of oscillatory predator-prey structures compared to random parameter baselines.
card.limitation: The loss function is indirect and hand-designed, rather than derived from a direct trajectory matching method.

slides.title: Adaptive Turn-Taking for Real-time Multi-Party Voice Agents
slides.highlight: This work introduces ModeratorLM, which uses role-playing and reasoning to improve turn-taking precision and reduce interruptions in multi-party conversations, contributing to HyECHO's goals in listener modeling and engagement.

card.one_liner: ModeratorLM is a role-playing voice agent that adapts turn-taking behavior based on explicitly assigned conversational roles.
card.key_idea: A speech LLM processing streaming audio chunks, using role-conditioned fine-tuning and an optional chain-of-thought reasoning variant (ModeratorLM-Think) to decide when to intervene in multi-party conversations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on real-world meeting data (NSF-1) and synthetic RolePlayConv dataset; showed >40% precision and >70% recall improvements over non-role-conditioned baselines.
card.limitation: The model relies heavily on textual transcriptions for decision-making, with performance degrading substantially when transcriptions are unavailable.

slides.title: Predicting Cognitive Load from Speech and Interaction Dynamics in Dyadic Conversations
slides.tldr: COGNITIVE LOAD PREDICTION FROM DYADIC SPEECH
slides.highlight: This research identifies how turn-taking dynamics and participation balance in dyadic conversations can predict cognitive load, supporting HyECHO's goals in modeling hybrid team states.

card.one_liner: Speech and interaction dynamics can predict perceived cognitive load in dyadic conversations as a regression task.
card.key_idea: A two-head GRU encoder predicts NASA-TLX scores using static acoustic features, temporal derivatives, and interaction features (e.g., turn-taking, speaking imbalance) from 53 dyads.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via Leave-One-Dyad-Out cross-validation on AVCAffe dataset using CCC, PCC, and RMSE. Results show modest, generalizable signals for temporal and mental demand.
card.limitation: Small sample size (53 dyads) limits sequence model capacity; labels are task-level rather than fine-grained temporal measures.

slides.title: Co-Creating Buildable and Open Social Robot Study Companions with University Students
slides.tldr: OPEN-SOURCE SOCIAL ROBOT DESIGN FOR ASSEMBLY
slides.highlight: This research explores how Design for Assembly and Disassembly can lower barriers for students building open-source social robots, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Applying DfA and DfD principles to open-source social robots improves usability and reduces perceived workload.
card.key_idea: Using the Double Diamond framework, the Robot Study Companion v4.1 was redesigned with twist-lock fasteners, snap-fit joints, and tool-free latches to simplify assembly and serviceability.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via two studies (developers and first-time builders) using SUS, NASA-TLX, and assembly timing. SUS rose from 59.4 to 89.4 for developers.
card.limitation: Small, non-random samples; potential self-evaluation bias from developers; lack of inter-rater reliability checks for thematic coding.

slides.title: Severance Hospital Launches Brain-Signal Controlled Wearable Humanoid Robot Project
slides.highlight: Severance Hospital is developing a wearable humanoid robot controlled by brain signals, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.
